POWER MECHANICS — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #6
====

GRADE: Grade 11
SUBJECT: POWER MECHANICS
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When learning Project, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Project.
   B. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Project.
   C. Skip safety briefings for Project.
   D. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Project.

2. ICT stands for: (1 mark)
   A. Information and Communication Technology
   B. Internal Cooking Timer
   C. International Cricket Team
   D. Input Cable Tester

3. When learning Orthographic projection, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Orthographic projection.
   B. Skip safety briefings for Orthographic projection.
   C. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Orthographic projection.
   D. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Orthographic projection.

4. When learning Principles of Power Mechanics, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Principles of Power Mechanics.
   B. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Principles of Power Mechanics.
   C. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Principles of Power Mechanics.
   D. Skip safety briefings for Principles of Power Mechanics.

5. When learning Limits, fits and tolerance, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Limits, fits and tolerance.
   B. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Limits, fits and tolerance.
   C. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Limits, fits and tolerance.
   D. Skip safety briefings for Limits, fits and tolerance.

6. When learning Isometric projection, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Isometric projection.
   B. Skip safety briefings for Isometric projection.
   C. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Isometric projection.
   D. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Isometric projection.

7. Before using a sharp tool in a workshop, you should: (1 mark)
   A. Remove all guards
   B. Work alone with eyes closed
   C. Run with the tool
   D. Wear safety gear and follow instructions

8. A computer’s main brain for processing is the: (1 mark)
   A. Speaker
   B. Keyboard
   C. Monitor
   D. CPU

9. When learning ISO Thread forms, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Leave sharp tools on the floor after ISO Thread forms.
   B. Guess wiring or cutting steps for ISO Thread forms.
   C. Skip safety briefings for ISO Thread forms.
   D. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for ISO Thread forms.

10. Electricity safety rule: (1 mark)
   A. Ignore burnt cables
   B. Overload every socket
   C. Insert metal objects into sockets for fun
   D. Never touch live wires with wet hands

11. When learning Suspension system, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Suspension system.
   B. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Suspension system.
   C. Skip safety briefings for Suspension system.
   D. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Suspension system.

12. When learning Steering system, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Skip safety briefings for Steering system.
   B. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Steering system.
   C. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Steering system.
   D. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Steering system.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Petrol Fuel System and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Principles of Power Mechanics and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Health and safety in a power mechanics work environment and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Metalwork processes in power mechanics and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. A — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Project.

2. A — Information and Communication Technology

3. C — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Orthographic projection.

4. A — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Principles of Power Mechanics.

5. A — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Limits, fits and tolerance.

6. C — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Isometric projection.

7. D — Wear safety gear and follow instructions

8. D — CPU

9. D — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for ISO Thread forms.

10. D — Never touch live wires with wet hands

11. B — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Suspension system.

12. D — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Steering system.

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Petrol Fuel System; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Principles of Power Mechanics; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Health and safety in a power mechanics work environment; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Metalwork processes in power mechanics; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
